propositions: Duplicated computations exist in 2–7 locations across the codebase; when a fix lands in one copy, its twins remain broken, causing families of related tickets

The consolidation approach collapses each duplicated computation into a single shared module and pins behaviour with construct-uniqueness guards that assert distinctive atoms, not implementation details

Acceptance criterion AC3 (net non-test lines negative) fails empirically; consolidation work correctly relocates duplicated bodies into documented owner modules, which increases line count despite shrinking call sites

Acceptance criterion AC2 (tests-only-additions) fails for 9 of 23 children; the failures are legitimate consolidation outcomes (deleted test-side duplicates, re-pointed references to owners) that do not change pinned observable behaviour
Thirteen consolidation children and nine hardening children are scoped to collapse hotspots across store paths, commands, engine reconciler, LLM, and MCP modules

AC2 and AC3 require restatement to measure actual consolidation guarantees (exactly one implementation per construct, no pinned behaviour changes) rather than proxies that correct consolidation work violates
